rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is eternally one, incapable of duplication, disappearance, or change, with no equal, counterpart, likeness, or rival in any relation.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ, ikileşmesi veya yok olması veya değişmesi imkân ve ihtimâli olmayan hep birdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To affirm divine oneness one must negate every other deity universally; the formula uses lā of generic negation, not a particular denial like laysa.
rows.anchor: O’ndan başka hiçbir ilâh yoktur” diye mâ‘adâyı nefy-i küllî ile nefyetmek îcab eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal force is also expressed by min in 5:73 and innamā in 4:171.
rows.anchor: nefiyde istiğrak için “min” getirilmiştir. إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating ahad in affirmation and negation establishes divine oneness and excludes any matching unity or plurality.
rows.anchor: İşte “ehad”in bir isbatta bir de nefiyde olarak iki defa zikrinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God has necessary, true existence; all other beings are contingent and depend on Him for existence and permanence.
rows.anchor: Hepsi vücud ve bekāda hep O’na muhtaçtır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creatures may unite, divide, generate, and oppose one another, but only through God's gift and permission; His providence and judgment resolve their disputes and establish right.
rows.anchor: Fakat hiçbirisi kendiliklerinden değil, hepsi Allah’ın vergisi, müsaadesi iledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, this world, and the next rest on God's oneness and subsist through His self-sufficiency, subject to His command.
rows.anchor: Bütün semâvât ve Arzıyla âlem, dünya ve âhiret O’nun ehadiyetine müstenid, samediyetiyle kāim

rows.speaker: Enes ve Übey
rows.claim: A report says the heavens and earth are founded upon this surah.
rows.anchor: Enes’ten ve Übey’den rivayet olunduğu üzere bütün semâvât ve Arz’ın bu sûre üzerine müesses olduğu zikredilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the surah's equivalence to the whole Quran by its concise presentation of God's attributes, justice, and oneness.
rows.anchor: teâlâ’nın sıfâtı ve adl ü tevhîdi üzere dürüldüğü içindir.

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Knowledge of tawhid is exalted because its subject is God; those who belittle it show weak knowledge, little reverence, and disregard for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Her kim onu istihfaf ve istihkār ederse mâlumuna ilminin zaafından, O’na tâziminin azlığından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı infers that a Prophetic report says Qul huwa Allahu ahad is equivalent to the whole Quran.
rows.anchor: diye bir hadîs-i nebevî rivayet edilmiş demektir.

rows.speaker: Enes
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari transmits a report urging nightly recitation because the surah equals the whole Quran.
rows.anchor: İbnü’l- Enbârî Mesâhif’te Hazret-i Enes’ten şöyle tahric eylemiştir: مَا يَمْنَعُ أَحدَكُمْ

rows.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd
rows.claim: A Musnad report through Ibn Lahi'a is uncertain whether the surah equals half or one third; most raised and companion reports specify one third.
rows.anchor: bir rivayette de “nısfına veya

rows.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd
rows.claim: The Prophet asks whether anyone can read one third of the Quran in a night and says this surah equals that portion; the passage cites several transmitters and companions.
rows.anchor: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ okur o, Kur’ân’ın sülüsüne mu‘âdil olur” (Ahmed Müsned’de, Buhârî, Ebû Ya‘lâ, Ebû Sa‘îd’den

rows.speaker: Ebu’d-Derdâ
rows.claim: The Prophet says God divided the Quran into three portions and made this surah one of them.
rows.anchor: üç cüze ayırdı, قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ’i Kur’ân’ın cüzlerinden bir cüz kıldı” (Ahmed, Müslim, Ebu’d-Derdâ’dan)

rows.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd
rows.claim: The Prophet swears that Qul huwa Allahu ahad is equivalent to one third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: Nefsim yedinde olan Allah’a kasem ederim o, yani قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ Kur’ân’ın sülüsüne mu‘âdil olur

rows.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
rows.claim: After gathering people and reciting the surah, the Prophet explains that it is equivalent to one third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: işte o Kur’ân’ın sülüsüne mu‘âdil olur

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: A report says that anyone who recites Qul huwa Allahu ahad Allah al-Samad has read one third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: Her kim قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ okursa Kur’ân’ın sülüsünü okumuştur” (Taberânî, İbn Ömer’den)

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: A report likens one recitation to one third, two to two thirds, and three to the whole Quran.
rows.anchor: bir kere قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ okursa Kur’ân’ın sülüsünü okumuş gibidir, iki kere okursa Kur’ân’ın sülüsânını

rows.speaker: müfessirîn ve ulemânın bir kısmı
rows.claim: One scholarly view takes equivalence to one third as equivalence in meaning rather than reward, citing the hadith that divides the Quran into three parts.
rows.anchor: Murad sevâbı itibariyle değil, mânası itibariyle üçte birine mu‘âdil olmasıdır demişler

rows.speaker: müfessirîn ve ulemânın bir kısmı
rows.claim: One rationale divides Quranic meanings into tawhid, legislation, and ethical refinement; this surah explains tawhid, the foundation of the other two.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın me‘ânîsi üç ilme râci‘olur: İlm-i tevhid, ilm-i teşrî‘, ilm-i tehzîb-i ahlâk.

rows.speaker: müfessirîn ve ulemânın bir kısmı
rows.claim: Another rationale says the Quran comprises creed, rulings, and stories, while this surah concerns creed alone.
rows.anchor: Kur’an bir bakıma akāid, ahkâm, kısas bu üçünü müştemildir, bu sûre ise hep akāide müte‘alliktir.

rows.speaker: Gazzâlî
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali divides Quranic sciences into knowledge of origin, return, and the straight path between them, and assigns this surah to the origin and thus one third.
rows.anchor: Mebde’e ilim, me‘âda ilim, bu ikisi arasındaki sırât-ı müstakīme ilim.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı objects that God is both First and Last, return to Him and the straight path toward Him are also signaled, so this scheme would make the surah equivalent to all three parts.
rows.anchor: Allah sade mebde’den ibaret değil, Evvel ve Âhir’dir.

rows.speaker: ulemâ
rows.claim: Another rationale identifies three foundations of faith: knowing God, affirming the Prophet's truth, and believing in standing before God in the afterlife; this surah covers one.
rows.anchor: Allah’a marifet, Peygamber’in sıdkını itiraf, âhirette Allah’ın huzûrunda kıyâma itikaddır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Equivalence to one third and equivalence to the whole Quran need not conflict, since tawhid is the root and the rest serves it.
rows.anchor: tevhid bunların hepsinin aslı ve mâ‘adâsı onun vesâilidir.

rows.speaker: ulemâdan diğer bir kısım
rows.claim: Another scholarly view reads the hadiths literally: the surah equals one third of the Quran in reward.
rows.anchor: murad sevab itibariyle sülüsüne mu‘âdil olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: An objection cites the report that every Quranic letter earns ten good deeds, so reading the whole Quran should yield far more reward.
rows.anchor: her harfine on hasene vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer distinguishes detailed letter-by-letter reward from the holistic reward for completing the Quran; the surah equals one third of the latter, not the former.
rows.anchor: Kur’an okuyan için iki türlü sevab vardır; birisi her harfine göre verilen tafsîlî sevab

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı illustrates the distinction with a builder paid daily and also given a completion bonus.
rows.anchor: binâyı bitirdiği zaman da yevmiye ücretinden başka bir de bahşiş verir.

rows.speaker: Kirmânî
rows.claim: Kirmânī says the comparison concerns the basis of reward, not its extra amount; ninefold additional reward accounts for the greater labor of reading one third.
rows.anchor: Teşbih aslındadır, ziyadesinde değildir, dokuzu ziyade meşakkat mukabilindedir.

rows.speaker: Şihâb-ı Hafâcî
rows.claim: Al-Hafaji distinguishes contemplative reading from reading without understanding; careful recitation of subtle meanings may equal a third lacking contemplation or knowledge of God and tawhid.
rows.anchor: Her kim bunu edâsının hukūkuna riayet ederek ve ince mânalarını anlayarak okursa böyle teemmül ve tedebbür

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says divine generosity can award easier worship more reward than harder worship, including special rewards for particular times or places; the wisdom belongs to God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın mahz-ı keremiyle çok bir meşakkat olmayan bazı ibadetler yine o cinsten kat kat meşakkatli olanların sevâbından daha çok bir sevab tahsis buyurmuş olmasına mâni‘yoktur.

rows.speaker: İbn Abdilberr
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says silence is safer and better than speaking about the issue; Elmalılı agrees this is sound while retaining the importance of al-Kashshaf's alert.
rows.anchor: bu meselede sükût kelâmdan efdal ve eslem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's subject is God in His divinity and His relation to creation, especially rational beings and human servitude.
rows.anchor: ilm-i Kur’ân’ın mevzû‘u, ulûhiyeti haysiyetiyle Allah teâlâ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatiha introduces this subject, while Ikhlas gives God's own definition of Himself and the support on which Quranic knowledge rests; it is therefore a Quranic epitome and equivalent.
rows.anchor: bu sûre de Allah teâlâ’nın kendi bir târifi olmak itibariyle bütün ilm-i Kur’ân’ın kāim olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran can be considered as Fatiha, a middle, and an ending; its ending is Ikhlas with the two refuge surahs.
rows.anchor: Hâtime de İhlâs ile mu‘avvizeteyndir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacred hadith divides Fatiha between God and the servant in three parts: three verses for God, one shared verse, and three for servants; Ikhlas addresses God alone while the refuge surahs concern servants, making Ikhlas akin to half or one third.
rows.anchor: birinci kısım üç âyet ile yalnız Allah’a ait, ikinci kısım bir âyet إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers who grasp the meanings and relations gain corresponding detailed reward, while those reciting with general faith gain corresponding holistic reward; the Quran's wording conveys meaning and reward is attached to recitation.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde bunların mânalarındaki incelikleri ve münasebetleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise of tenfold reward per good deed and His freedom to decree as He wills permit special reward for Ikhlas equivalent to all, half, or a third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trying to understand Ikhlas and act on it adds further good deeds; using tafsir and translation to understand and convey meanings and rulings is itself intended.
rows.anchor: tefsir ve meal ile mânayı ve ahkâmı anlamaya ve anlatmaya çalışmadan da matlub budur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many further virtue reports exist, some strong and some weak; some call Ikhlas the best surah, though its non-obligatory status in prayer makes that claim not fully concordant with Fatiha's required status.
rows.anchor: hadisler de mervîdir, içlerinde kavî olanlar

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says sound reports suffice to establish the surah's virtue and that it has even been called the best Quranic surah.
rows.anchor: Bunun hakkında vârid olan ehâdîs-i sahîha fazlına kâfidir, hatta Kur’an’daki sûrelerin efdali bile denilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Safvân-i Külâ‘î
rows.claim: Alusi reports that a narration from Safwan al-Kula'i is used to identify Ikhlas as the greatest Quran surah.
rows.anchor: Safvân-i Külâ‘î’den rivayet olunan şu hadis ile istidlâl edenler de olmuştur

rows.speaker: Ukbe b. Âmir
rows.claim: The Prophet offers to teach three best surahs found in earlier scriptures and the Quran: Ikhlas, Falaq, and Nas, then tells Uqba to recite them with Tabbet nightly.
rows.anchor: Ukbe b. Âmir’den, demiştir ki: ‘Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bana: «Tevrat’ta ve İncil’de ve Zebur’da ve Kur’ân-ı Azîm’de bulunan sûrelerin hayırlısı üç sûreyi öğreteyim mi sana?»

rows.speaker: Tirmizî
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits part of the Uqba report and grades it hasan; Alusi says it establishes these as among the best, not necessarily the single best.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî de bu hadîsin bir kısmını rivayet etmiş ve hasen demiştir.

rows.speaker: İbn Hassâd
rows.claim: Ibn Hassad is astonished that anyone denies differences in merit despite the many transmitted proofs.
rows.anchor: Bu babda vârid olan nusûsun kesreti ile beraber fazlda ihtilâfı inkâr edene ta‘accüb olunur.

rows.speaker: tafdîle kāil olanlar
rows.claim: One explanation makes superior merit depend on the reader's spiritual responses, contemplation of the first attributes, and reverent awe.
rows.anchor: Fazl, nefsin intikālâtı ve evsâf-ı ûlâyı tedebbür ve haşyeti itibariyle sevâbın büyüklüğüne

rows.speaker: tafdîle kāil olanlar
rows.claim: Another explanation ties merit to the wording's meaning: Ikhlas contains extraordinary indications of divine oneness and attributes absent from Tabbet.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i İhlâs’ın tazammun ettiği meselâ vahdâniyet ve sıfât-ı ilâhiyeye delâlet, meselâ Tebbet’te mevcud değildir

rows.speaker: Halîmî naklen Beyhakī
rows.claim: One basis for preference is greater practical necessity: commands, prohibitions, promises, and warnings are more needed than stories, which reinforce them.
rows.anchor: emir ve nehiy ve va‘d ü va‘îd âyetleri kısas âyetlerinden daha hayırlıdır denilir.

rows.speaker: Halîmî naklen Beyhakī
rows.claim: A second basis is that verses naming God, describing His attributes, and displaying His majesty rank higher than verses without these.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın esmâsını ta‘dâd ve sıfâtını beyan ve azamet ve celâline delâlet eyleyen âyetlere

rows.speaker: Halîmî naklen Beyhakī
rows.claim: A third basis is immediate benefit: reciting Ayat al-Kursi, Ikhlas, or the refuge surahs brings refuge and devotional reliance at once, whereas legal verses yield knowledge but do not enact a ruling by recitation.
rows.anchor: Âyete’l-Kürsî, İhlâs, Mu‘avvizeteyn gibi ki bunlarda Allah teâlâ’yı yüksek sıfatlarıyla zikir bulunduğundan

rows.speaker: Halîmî naklen Beyhakī
rows.claim: A fourth basis is God's devotional apportionment of multiplied recitation reward, even where its reason is hidden, as with favored times and places.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ onun kıraatini diğerlerininkinin kat kat kıraati gibi kılmış ve ona diğerlerine vermediği sevâbı vermiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preference on any of these grounds does not deny that all Quranic passages are God's speech and equal in that shared respect; Elmalılı quotes 39:23.
rows.anchor: tafdil hepsinin kelâmullah olması itibariyle müsâvî ve ona nisbette müttehid olmalarına münâfî olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah concludes a sequence: Fatiha announces tawhid and prophethood; later surahs describe Muhammad's good end and his opponents' ruin, then Ikhlas removes all traces of shirk and affirms pure knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: bu sûre-i celîlede sırr-ı tevhid her şâibeden ârî, her şüpheden âzâde hâlis bir îkān ile tâlim ve telkin olunarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhlas teaches that God neither begets nor is begotten and has no equal; all else depends on His oneness and self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın doğurmaz, doğurulmaz ve hiçbir vechile küfvü bulunmaz ehadiyet ve samediyet ile tanınması lüzûmu bildirilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all beings, including the Prophet, face harm from others, the final refuge is God: after Fatiha's plea for worship, help, and guidance, the two final refuge surahs command seeking His protection from outward and inward evil.
rows.anchor: son çâre-i selâmet O’na esmâ-i hüsnâsıyla ilticâ ederek sığınmaktan ibaret olduğu ber vech-i âtî biri âfâkī biri enfüsî iki sığınma sûresi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heading identifies Surah al-Falaq as Medinan and five verses long.
rows.anchor: سُورَةُ الْفَلَقِ مَدَنِيَّةٌ وَهِيَ خَمْسُ اٰيَاتٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Quranic recitation is commanded by qul, the reciter should preserve it as written and transmitted; omitting it may suit a bare supplication, while Kafirun requires it and Tabbet omits it.
rows.anchor: aynen okunmalıdır, çünkü mushaflarda öyle tesbit edilmiş, öyle vârid olmuştur.

rows.speaker: İmam Ebû Mansûr Mâtürîdî
rows.claim: Al-Maturidi says the command applies to every person under the same religious obligation, not only the Prophet addressed.
rows.anchor: bununla me’mur olan yalnız muhatabdan ibaret değil, onun gibi mükellef olan herkestir.

rows.speaker: bir görüş
rows.claim: Another view says each reader is the one commanded, so everyone should tell themselves to make this supplication and not abandon it.
rows.anchor: Bununla me’mur, okuyanın kendisidir. Allah teâlâ bu suretle şunu bildirmiştir ki bu mazmûnun makāmında herkes kendisine bunu söylemeyi emretsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refuge surahs are recited as an instruction to say the prayer both to oneself and to others.
rows.anchor: kendine ve herkese şöyle dua etmeyi söyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isti'aza means seeking another's protection against harm; the passage names the refuge seeker, the one sought for refuge, the harm fled, and the means and protector.
rows.anchor: bir fenalıktan korunmak için gayra ilticâ etmek, himayesini istemektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falak is a rich word rooted in splitting; its root denotes splitting or cracking, while the fatha form names what emerges from that split rather than the crack itself.
rows.anchor: en esaslı mânası yarmak mefhûmunu mutazammın olmak hasebiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image is a seed split open, with a bud, leaf, water, light, or other created thing appearing between its two sides.
rows.anchor: O çatlağın iki şıkkı arasından netice olarak pürtleyip beliren, inkişaf ve inbisat eden tomurcuk, yaprak veya su veya ışık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran 6:95–96 depicts God splitting seed and kernel, bringing life from death and death from life, and splitting dawn; Rabb al-Falaq thus evokes creator and nurturer of all that emerges.
rows.anchor: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَالِقُ ٱلْحَبِّ وَٱلنَّوَىٰ يُخْرِجُ ٱلْحَىَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَيِّتِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also conveys astonishing speed, novelty, pressure, and intensity, reflected in words for racing, invention, a brilliant poet, marvels, and calamities.
rows.anchor: bir sür‘at ve şâyân-ı ta‘accüb bir bedâ‘at ve bir tazyik ve şiddet mânası dahi bulunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One lexical sense is all creatures emerging from nonexistence, including springs, rain, plants, descendants, and children; as created and needy, falak contrasts with Samad.
rows.anchor: ‘Ademden yarılıp çıkan halk, yani ale’l-umûm mahlûkāt ve bâhusus dağlardan pınarlar, buluttan yağmurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In common usage falak means dawn, the light opening from the dawn column or daybreak, and in this sense it contrasts with darkness called gasak.
rows.anchor: Örfte bilhassa sabaha, yahut amûd-i subuhtan münşak, yani amûd şeklinde mümted olan aydınlığa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other dictionary senses are a low, level place between two hills and the wooden stock placed on prisoners' feet.
rows.anchor: İki tepe beyninde vâki‘alçak, oturaklı düz yere denir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further senses include milk residue at the bottom of a bowl and curdled milk.
rows.anchor: Çanak dibinde kalan süt bakıyyesine denir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falak is also reported as a name for Hell or a well in Hell.
rows.anchor: Cehennemin veya cehennemde bir kuyunun ismi olduğu da menkuldür.

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Al-Raghib glosses falak as dawn, also as the rivers in Quran 27:61, and as the word God gave Moses by which he split the sea.
rows.anchor: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ subuhtur

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas ve sâire
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir records three interpretations attributed to Ibn Abbas and others: a prison, well, or Hell; dawn; and creation.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan ve sâireden üç rivayet kaydettikten sonra

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says Arab usage most clearly means dawn, though a prison named Falak in Hell is also possible; because the verse does not restrict the Lordship, every thing called falak is intended.
rows.anchor: kelâm-ı Arabda ‘felak’ ise felak-ı subuhtur

rows.speaker: İbn Münzir ve İbn Ebî Hâtim
rows.claim: Many exegetes prefer the broader sense creation; Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit this interpretation from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir ile İbn Ebî Hâtim de bunu İbn Abbas’tan rivayet etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Avicenna follows the broad sense, defining falak as the darkness of nonexistence split by the light of existence.
rows.anchor: vücud nûruyla yarılmış olan ‘adem zulmetidir demekle bu mâna üzere yürümüştür.

rows.speaker: Câbir b. Abdullah, İbn Zeyd, Mücâhid, Katâde ve İbn Cübeyr
rows.claim: Most exegetes take falak in its most common customary sense of dawn, yielding Rabb al-Falaq as Lord of the dawn.
rows.anchor: Câbir b. Abdullah ve İbn Zeyd ve Mücâhid ve Katâde ve İbn Cübeyr’den rivayet olunduğu üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn signifies light after darkness, relief after constriction, and opening after closure; seeking refuge from its Lord promises protection and strengthens hope, obedience, and earnest reliance.
rows.anchor: zulmet akabinde nûr, darlıktan sonra genişlik, kapanıklıktan sonra açılış mânalarını müş‘ir olmak hasebiyle

rows.speaker: bir görüş
rows.claim: Dawn is mentioned particularly because it models resurrection: homes resemble graves, sleep resembles death, and morning departures amid mixed fortunes recall resurrection and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: bilhassa “felak”ın zikri onun kıyamet gününden bir numûne olması hasebiyledir.

rows.speaker: Kādî
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says Rabb is especially apt because rescuing someone from harms is an act of nurturing.
rows.anchor: Burada بِرَبِّ ismi sâir esmâdan, yani ‘felak’a izâfeti câiz olan diğer esmâ-i ilâhiyenin hepsinden ziyade mevki‘indedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qadi's explanation is clearest under the universal creation interpretation because Rabb encompasses both seeker and feared object; under dawn it signals God's power to change states and remove distress.
rows.anchor: Çünkü müste‘îze de müste‘azün minhe de şâmildir

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Avicenna says creatures, like a child, depend on the First Principle's emanation; Rabb highlights that no possible being is self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: Merbub hâlâtının hiçbir şeyinde rabden müstağnî olamaz

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Avicenna further says when refuge fails, the cause lies in the recipient's capacity rather than any withholding by the First Principle, from whom all good flows.
rows.anchor: maksad hâsıl olmazsa onun ‘adem-i husûlü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's report about merciful breezes in a person's days urges people to present themselves for them; divine favors are constant, and deficiency lies in the recipient's readiness.
rows.anchor: Eltâf-ı rabbâniyenin nefehâtı dâim ve halel ancak müsta‘idden olduğunu beyan buyurmuştur.

rows.speaker: Abdullah b. Amr b. Âs
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet explained al-Falaq as a prison in Hell where tyrants and the arrogant are confined, from which Hell itself seeks God's protection.
rows.anchor: Abdullah b. Amr b. Âs’tan şöyle tahric eylemiştir; demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Amr b. Abese
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet calls al-Falaq a well in Hell; when it is heated Hell heats up and suffers from it as humans suffer from Hell.
rows.anchor: İbn Merdûye Amr b. Abese’den

rows.speaker: Ka‘b
rows.claim: Ka'b says al-Falaq is a house in Hell whose opening makes its inhabitants cry out from its intense heat.
rows.anchor: Ka‘b’dan da şöyle tahrîc etmişlerdir: “Felak cehennemde bir evdir

rows.speaker: Kelbî
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi calls al-Falaq a valley in Hell; another reported interpretation identifies it with Hell itself.
rows.anchor: Kelbî’den de: “Felak cehennemde bir vâdidir” diye rivayet edilmiş ve cehennemin kendisidir de denilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf derives the Hell sense from the word for an expansive low plain, with plural fulkan, like halak and hulkan.
rows.anchor: engin arza “felak” denilmesinden me’huzdur, bunun cem‘i “fülkān” gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord of this Hell punishment promises rescue from the greatest danger, just as the dawn sense offers hope of relief.
rows.anchor: azâbın en büyüğüne işaret ile ondan isti‘âze edene tahlîsin vaadini tazammun eyler

rows.speaker: bazı ashâb-ı kirâm
rows.claim: Some Companions in Syria dismissed the worldly comfort of protected non-Muslims by asking whether al-Falaq awaited them afterward, alluding to Ka'b's Hell interpretation.
rows.anchor: Şam’a gelip de ehl-i zimmetin dünya maîşetindeki vüs‘at ve refahlarını gördüğü zaman

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi prefers the broadest sense: all possible beings split into existence, especially springs from mountains, rain from clouds, plants from earth, and children from wombs.
rows.anchor: ‘Felak’ın bu üç mânasından benim nazarımda tereccuh eden evvelki e‘am mânasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under this reading al-Falaq means creation and contrasts with Samad; the previous surah's self-sufficient Creator is unlike dependent, generated, changing, and perishing creatures.
rows.anchor: “felak” “samed”in hilâfı ve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı first preferred a literal translation as Lord of created nature and all creation, but then chose to retain falak because it clearly includes every object of the term and preserves its breadth and nuance.
rows.anchor: “sığınırım Rabbine o fıtratın, şerrinden bütün hilkatın” ilh... diye terceme etmek fikr-i âcizâneme lafzen ve mânen münâsib gelmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma khalaq means every creature capable of evil and every kind of harm: material or spiritual, worldly or otherworldly, outward or inward, natural or chosen.
rows.anchor: Herhangisi olursa olsun şer şânından olan mahlûkātın kâffesinin şerrinden, ki maddî ve mânevî, dünyevî ve uhrevî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The list includes humans, jinn, devils, animals, insects, microbes, poison, fire, sins, passions, the self, and one's deeds; the sought refuge concerns harms directed toward the seeker.
rows.anchor: ins ü cin ile bütün şeytanların şerrine, sibâ‘u hevâm ve haşerat ve mikropların şerrine

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ ve bazıları
rows.claim: Avicenna and others argue the human soul cannot be among the evil sought against, so ma khalaq must mean bodies and material things, since the soul belongs to the command-world rather than created world.
rows.anchor: İbn Sînâ gibi bazıları burada isti‘âze eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects that limitation: the spirit is created and the seeker is included among creatures, so refuge covers inner harms chosen, habitual, or mistaken as well as external harms; Quran 4:79 and a hadith warn against the self.
rows.anchor: doğrusu rûh da mahluktur, müste‘îzin kendisi de mâhalakta dâhildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two verses summarize the themes of both refuge surahs; following them, the surah specifies especially frequent dangers, moving from outward to inward evils.
rows.anchor: bu iki âyet, bu iki sûre mecmû‘unun bütün mazmûnunu câmi‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghasik when it enters can mean a dark thing as it sets in, penetrates, or descends.
rows.anchor: vukūbu sıra yani girip daldığı, yahut bastığı, veya battığı zaman.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gasak, gusuk, and gasekan relate to intense darkness, fullness, flowing, discharge, cold, and foul smell, with filling, flowing, or pouring as common roots.
rows.anchor: şiddetli karanlık, dolgunluk, akmak, dökülmek soğukluk ve kokarlık mânalarıyla alâkadardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gasak may mean the night growing dark or the onset of darkness, contrasting with falak in the phrase from nightfall until dawn.
rows.anchor: مِنَ الْغَسَقِ إِلَى الْفَلَقِ “gasaktan felaka kadar” denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other meanings include a blight beetle in grain and a dim, smoky, or watering eye.
rows.anchor: Buğday içinde bulunan karacaya da “gasak” ıtlak edilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gasekan can name discharge such as wound fluid, drizzle, milk, or any pouring liquid.
rows.anchor: yaradan sarı su akmasına ve buluttan yağmur çisemesine ve memeden süt dökülmesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gasak and gassaq also describe extremely cold, foul-smelling drink or water; the Quran uses gassaq this way in 78:25.
rows.anchor: İçilemeyecek derecede gayet soğuk ve fena kokulu (bârid ve müntin) içki veya suya “gasak” ve “gassâk” denilir. Nitekim إِلَّا حَمِيمًۭا وَغَسَّاقًۭا [en-Nebe’ 78/25] bundandır.

rows.speaker: Kāmûs mütercimi
rows.claim: The Kamus translator says Turkish uses gasak for cold, foul water, while Cevâlîkī supposes the Arabic term was borrowed from Turkish; Elmalılı finds the reverse more apparent but does not know that Turkish sense, noting only resemblance to gasık, sexual desire, a major evil.
